name: The Federation Prime Contractor
tagline: Coordinate candidate partner work through explicit artifacts, acceptance, and owner gates.
mission: Run a prime's own program, partner-discovery, integration, quality, and change-control teams around a synthetic offline maker-hall intake engagement. Split proposed work among three discoverable organization seeds, integrate only local public-reference fixtures, and rehearse rejection and rework without activating a federation or claiming partner authority.

teams.name: Customer Delivery and Program Office
teams.purpose: Own the fictional engagement scope, deliverable sequence, and conditional owner handoff.

teams.name: Partner Discovery and Briefs
teams.purpose: Prepare bounded discovery-only briefs for three candidate organizations without outreach, contracts, or workspace registration.

teams.name: Artifact Integration
teams.purpose: Maintain the public data interface and assemble only inert local synthetic fixtures for review.

teams.name: Acceptance and Quality
teams.purpose: Run the offline content checks, reject incompatible submissions, and distinguish fixture passes from real acceptance.

teams.name: Change Control and Risk
teams.purpose: Track rework, scope impacts, public-artifact boundaries, and the missing owner approvals.

case.title: Pocket Queue: a 60-attendee maker-hall intake rehearsal
case.brief: SYNTHETIC engagement for fictional Hearthstep Maker Hall. Propose an offline anonymous-ticket intake rehearsal: applied-invention-lab is a candidate for the prototype interface, enterprise-transformation-firm for the operating model, and product-launch-company for the operator pilot kit. They are DISCOVERY-ONLY candidates, not contracted or joined partners. The prime's five own team workspaces belong only to its own demonstration world. Included submissions are original local fixtures, not partner-delivered work.
success_criteria: Each of the three candidate organizations has a concrete machine-readable brief, scoped deliverable, dependency, and review gate.
The local matrix checks eighteen criteria across three reference artifacts and one derived integration report.
The baseline rejects the 1440-minute retention setting and the incompatible pilot-kit interface version, and blocks the integration report.

The corrected fixture passes content checks but still reports no exchange approval, contract, membership, workspace registration, federation activation, delivery authority, or real partner acceptance.
Only separately owner-approved public artifacts may cross independent organizations; this package performs no crossing or remote operation.

tasks.title: Freeze the synthetic engagement and own-world boundary
tasks.instructions: Define the fictional intake pilot, required artifacts, delivery sequence, and prime-only team scope. Explicitly separate discovery references from contracts, federation activation, and cross-world registration.
acceptance: Includes 60 synthetic attendees, a 120-minute retention ceiling, and the anonymous ticket field allowlist.
States that all five prime teams share only demo-federation-prime-contractor and no candidate workspace is registered there.
Contains no approved external effect or claim that a partner has agreed to work.

tasks.title: Prepare the prototype candidate discovery packet
tasks.instructions: Turn the applied-invention-lab brief into an owner-reviewable discovery request covering the local prototype interface and limitations. It is not a sent request or contract.
acceptance: Names the candidate slug and prototype-spec deliverable, interface fields, and exact acceptance criteria.
Labels the relationship discovery-only and the request unsent/unapproved; offers no remote authority.

tasks.title: Prepare the operating-model candidate packet
tasks.instructions: Prepare the enterprise-transformation-firm discovery request, explicitly depending on the reviewed prototype interface rather than a registered foreign workspace or assumed partner result.
acceptance: Includes greeter, queue-steward, and closeout-reviewer roles, a bounded stop condition, and retention no longer than 120 minutes.
States that only a separately owner-approved public artifact could satisfy the cross-organization handoff.

tasks.title: Prepare the operator pilot-kit candidate packet
tasks.instructions: Prepare the product-launch-company discovery request for a closed synthetic rehearsal kit. Carry the upstream interface and operating-model dependencies and prohibit public-launch claims.
acceptance: Requires at least four concrete operator steps, the exact interface version, SYNTHETIC disclosure, owner review, and no public launch.
Remains an unapproved discovery packet, not advertising authorization or partner activation.

tasks.title: Validate local fixture and dependency contracts
tasks.instructions: Run the authored utility tests and inspect the explicit deliverable/dependency/matrix inputs. Validate only local inert JSON; do not import code, contact a partner, or add a workspace pointer.
acceptance: Rejects unknown rules, duplicate artifacts, cycles, unknown candidates, and unexpected artifact fields.
Confirms an acyclic dependency chain from prototype to operating model and pilot kit to the prime's derived report.
Describes offline behavior flags as content declarations, not dynamic proof that a partner application works.

tasks.title: Rehearse incompatible-deliverable rejection
tasks.instructions: Run the baseline fixture through the content matrix. Record exact failed criteria, source locations, downstream blockage, and the fact that these are authored examples rather than real submissions.
acceptance: Prototype content passes, operating-model retention 1440 fails the 1–120 bound, pilot-kit interface version 0 fails version 1, and integration-report is blocked.
Captures the expected nonzero baseline CLI exit code and does not call a failed baseline a tool malfunction.
Reports delivery_authorized false and no cross-world effects.

tasks.title: Bound the rejection-to-rework cycle
tasks.instructions: Review the rejection report and original change/risk rows. Specify minimal corrections, affected dependents, and renewed review gates; do not silently weaken the acceptance matrix.
acceptance: Proposes retention 120 and interface version 1, retaining both original failures as evidence.
Identifies downstream pilot-kit/integration checks that must rerun.
Does not approve the separate request to increase attendance to 90 or alter owner authority.

tasks.title: Assemble the corrected local reference set
tasks.instructions: Use the included corrected fixture as a worked example, verify it against the bounded rework plan, and produce a proposed inert submission set. No actual partner artifact is fetched or exchanged.
acceptance: Contains exactly the three declared reference artifacts with SYNTHETIC classification, candidate slugs, public-reference-fixture visibility, and no exchange approval.
Carries no unknown payload fields, private content, executable partner code, remote locator, or workspace registration.

tasks.title: Rerun content acceptance after rework
tasks.instructions: Apply the same eighteen criteria to the proposed reference set and record derived dependency acceptance. Keep content validity separate from actual delivery, performance testing, and owner approval.
acceptance: All three corrected local fixtures and derived integration report satisfy content checks without changing the matrix.
The report still says delivery_authorized false, real_partner_submissions false, and no external effects.
Lists live usability, independent application verification, owner exchange approval, and commercial acceptance as unperformed.

tasks.title: Review candidate briefs and public-artifact boundary
tasks.instructions: Compare every discovery packet and acceptance result to the boundary policy. Record missing approvals, risk owners, and why no passing fixture can activate a federation or authorize remote work.
acceptance: States that independent organizations retain separate worlds and only owner-approved public artifacts may cross.
Contains no foreign workspace registration, approved contract, membership, signing operation, federation activation, or delegated remote authority.
Identifies real outreach and artifact exchange as future separately approved work, not performed effects.

tasks.title: Issue the prime's conditional owner handoff
tasks.instructions: Join scope, candidate packets, rejection/rework evidence, and the boundary review into a proposed next-step decision. Distinguish a useful local rehearsal from an actual contracted delivery.
acceptance: Explains the demonstrated rejection/rework chain and the unresolved real delivery/performance questions.
Makes no activation, registration, contract, approved exchange, or real customer acceptance claim.
Any next external action is a bounded proposal requiring explicit owner approval.
